cohort: The study involved 144 singleton pregnancies resulting from oocyte donation and 144 singleton pregnancies resulting from IVF using autologous oocytes, all of which were achieved after fresh embryo transfer and resulted in delivery beyond 22 gestational weeks.
finding: Singleton pregnancies after oocyte donation were associated with a significantly higher risk for preeclampsia, pregnancy-induced hypertension, and caesarean delivery compared with pregnancies using autologous oocytes.
